correctness.rationale: The multinomial-to-independent-Poisson limit holds jointly on four distinct vertex neighborhoods under uniform arclength sampling, also for angles tending to pi/2. First-order distance losses along incident edges yield a minimum of two independent exponentials with rates summing exactly to one after normalization, hence one Exp(1) per endpoint and independent Gamma(2,1) per diagonal. Uniform localization excludes all other vertex pairs and controls Taylor errors. Exact diagonal separation converges to tau, giving the stated min of shifted Gamma laws. A deterministic nearest-boundary-point bound yields an exponential moment envelope, establishing convergence of all fixed moments; survival integration yields both exact limiting moments. Reproducible code checks exact endpoint reduction, detuning expansion, survival integrals and sample simulations.

value.rationale: The complete limiting distribution resolves a natural unstable geometric extreme: both diagonals compete in a rectangle, but arbitrarily small perturbations become decisive at sample-size scale 1/n. The mean interpolates explicitly from 5/4 to 2, all integer moments are controlled, and the entire law unexpectedly loses all dependence on rectangle aspect ratio by exact cancellation of edge-length sampling rates. This is a structural singular-crossover theorem, not routine fixed-shape asymptotics.
